3.name: Moon's Inspiration
3.notes:
The moon's primal magic enhances your Bardic Inspiration.

Inspired Eclipse: When you give a creature a Bardic Inspiration die as a Bonus Action, you can become Invisible and teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. Invisibility lasts until the start of your next turn or ends early after you make an attack roll, deal damage, or cast a spell.

Lunar Vitality: Once per turn when you restore Hit Points with a spell, you can expend a Bardic Inspiration die to increase the healing by a roll of that die. The healed creature's Speed increases by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.

3.name: Primal Lore
3.notes:
You learn Druidic and one Druid cantrip, which counts as a Bard spell for you but doesn't count against your cantrips known. You can replace this cantrip whenever you gain a Bard level.

You also gain proficiency in one skill: Animal Handling, Insight, Medicine, Nature, Perception, or Survival.

6.name: Blessing of Moonlight
6.notes:
You always have Moonbeam prepared.

When you cast Moonbeam, you may choose to glow faintly while the spell is active, shedding Dim Light in a 5-foot radius. When a creature fails its saving throw against this Moonbeam, another creature you can see within 60 feet regains 2d4 Hit Points.

You can modify Moonbeam this way once per Long Rest.

14.name: Eventide's Splendor
14.notes:
Your connection to lunar magic strengthens, improving Moon's Inspiration.

Shadow of the New Moon: When you use Inspired Eclipse, the creature who received Bardic Inspiration also becomes Invisible and can immediately use its Reaction to teleport up to 30 feet. It remains Invisible until the start of its next turn.

Vibrance of the Full Moon: When you use Lunar Vitality, you can roll 1d6 instead of expending a Bardic Inspiration die.
